SWP-013.title: Community Needs Assessment
SWP-013.outcome: Plan and conduct a participatory assessment that identifies needs, assets, and priorities.

modules.title: Assessment design
modules.focus: purpose, stakeholders, ethics, inclusion, and mixed-method choices

modules.title: Collecting and interpreting evidence
modules.focus: surveys, interviews, focus groups, asset mapping, and data quality

modules.title: Prioritisation and communication
modules.focus: ranking needs, validating findings, reporting back, and action recommendations

SWP-014.title: Community Organizing & Coalition Building
SWP-014.outcome: Mobilise communities and partners around shared, achievable goals.

modules.title: Organising foundations
modules.focus: power analysis, community leadership, issue selection, and trust building

modules.title: Coalition formation
modules.focus: partners, roles, governance, communication, conflict management, and inclusion

modules.title: Campaign action
modules.focus: strategy, tactics, mobilisation, evaluation, and sustainability

SWP-015.title: Program Development & Evaluation
SWP-015.outcome: Design a feasible community programme and measure whether it works.

modules.title: Programme design
modules.focus: needs-to-goals chain, theory of change, target groups, and feasibility

modules.title: Implementation planning
modules.focus: activities, budget assumptions, partnerships, risk management, and inclusion

modules.title: Monitoring and evaluation
modules.focus: indicators, baseline, data collection, learning loops, and reporting

items.prompt: A fictional needs assessment uses only coalition leaders' views and announces the result as the whole community's priority. Give five corrections addressing assessment and organising.
items.model_answer: Clarify the assessment purpose and inclusion/ethics; identify absent perspectives and suitable participatory methods without unsafe recruitment; consider assets alongside needs; validate and prioritise findings with an honest account of uncertainty; and explain coalition roles, power and communication so leaders do not stand for everyone. Do not invent a retained-course protocol.

items.model_answer: Provide accessible bounded entry and a response owner; address conflicts through an authorised impartial route; use designated qualified safeguarding/emergency arrangements where applicable; minimise information with realistic confidentiality/non-retaliation arrangements and review options; and interpret counts cautiously because access and recording can change. Facilitation is not investigation or adjudication.

items.prompt: Develop a conditional plan for a fictional community learning programme. A needs exercise hears only association leaders; the coalition disagrees on priorities; the hall has an access fee; unpaid work is requested before funding; a complaint route has no response owner; and delivery has not been approved. Integrate all eight PCEI courses. Explain evidence, participation, assets, accountability, inclusive options, implementation, review and boundaries.
items.model_answer: A coherent answer uses participatory assessment with assets/needs and validated priorities; examines coalition power, roles and communication; states a feasible theory of change and output/outcome indicators without causal overclaim; bounds dialogue influence and provides access/feedback; checks voluntary asset contributions and uncertainty; assigns impartial complaint handling with qualified safeguarding routes; compares inclusive options and records revisions; and sets conditional task owners, dependencies, simulation status and supervised-learning limits. Include appropriate authority, privacy and missing perspectives rather than collect real sensitive accounts.

rubric.scoring: 0 absent/unsafe; 1 relevant limited point; 2 defensible applied reasoning with an important gap; 3 coherent contextual reasoning with feasible action, authority and evidence limits. Accept equivalent defensible reasoning.

items.prompt: Critique a fictional programme that claims success from attendance, an asset list, fewer complaints and a praised prototype. Its coalition calls silence unanimous consent; one channel is app-only; it promises a completed field placement and certification after an offline quiz. Propose justified corrections across all eight PCEI courses and explain what evidence and approvals remain missing.
items.model_answer: A strong critique distinguishes assessment evidence and missing perspectives, coalition authority and consent, programme outputs and outcomes, dialogue access and disagreement, asset control and contribution burdens, grievance access/recording and qualified scope, prototype usability versus effects, and introductory rehearsal versus real delivery/competence. It sets feasible owners and feedback/revision points without assuming causal benefit. It rejects real sensitive coursework, unapproved recruitment, invented approvals and offline certification; approved courses, verified ParaLearn passes, full mixed exam, human written marking, independent moderation and authorised signatures remain separate gates.
